unit_name: 17th SS Panzergrenadier Division Götz von Berlichingen
current_activity: moving up to block US westward thrust near Carentan
notes: Ordered 7 June to move against airborne threat; forward elements reached assembly areas southwest of Carentan by 11 June; made contact with US paratroopers 10 June; Ostendorff's division assigned the primary mission of blocking westward thrust under II Parachute Corps.

unit_name: 17th SS Panzergrenadier Division Götz von Berlichingen
composing_text: SS-Panzergrenadier Regiment 37; SS-Panzergrenadier Regiment 38; GER-KG-HEINTZ (battle group from the 275th Division; after its arrival, CMH ch. IX)
notes: Counter-attacked 101st Airborne at dawn 13 June with armour (Bloody Gulch); repulsed with 2nd Armored Division CCA help. [v5: battle group added to composing_units.] [Review item 2: the attachment of Kampfgruppe Heintz to this division is relation CR0374 (CMH ch. IX p. 378-379).]

unit_name: 17th SS Panzergrenadier Division Götz von Berlichingen
source_locator: R604: p. 81; R285: table of 1944 (July row)
current_activity: 17th SS Panzer Grenadier Division headquarters controls the Périers sector of the LXXXIV Corps right wing
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 5 p. 81 (the VII Corps attack of 4 July): "The Germans in the Périers sector, comprising part of the right (east) wing of the LXXXIV Corps, were under the local operational control of the headquarters of the 17th SS Panzer Grenadier Division"; one of its two regiments held positions below Carentan and the separate 6th Parachute Regiment was attached. Location: the Périers sector on the Carentan-Périers isthmus; the point is Périers, with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the source names the sector, not a command post. Relationship: the sector is part of the LXXXIV Corps right wing (ch. 5 p. 81); the Lexikon table gives the LXXXIV Corps for July; the earlier relation to the II Parachute Corps (CR0046) ends on 3 July, see the changelog. Location support: good: two source families agree on the corps.

unit_name: 17th SS Panzergrenadier Division Götz von Berlichingen
current_activity: 17th SS Panzer Grenadier Division, much weakened, defending the Périers area
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 12 p. 227 gives the German order of battle on the morning of 24 July 1944, the day before the Cobra bombardment: the considerably weakened forces of the 17th SS Panzer Grenadier Division defended in the Périers area with the 2d SS Panzer Division. Location: Périers area. Location approximate: the Green Book gives the sector, not the command post of the unit.

unit_name: 17th SS Panzergrenadier Division Götz von Berlichingen
current_activity: The 17th SS Panzer Grenadier Division refits in the Metz area behind the First Army front
notes: Event date: CMH Lorraine Campaign ch. 1 p. 47: "The 17th SS proceeded with the work of refitting and absorbing large numbers of replacements from the 49th and 51st SS Panzer Grenadier Brigades". Event definition: the refit in the first days of September; the passage follows the 1-2 September arrivals and precedes the description of the front "On 5 September", so 5 September is an approximate date. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Metz with a precision of 10 km, because the source says "the Metz area". Location approximate: a town point for the Metz area. Location support: CMH names the Metz area. Commander: unknown. Context: on 31 August two battalions of the division had formed an outpost line west of Metz.

unit_name: 17th SS Panzergrenadier Division Götz von Berlichingen
current_activity: The 17th SS Panzer Grenadier Division holds the First Army line at Sillegny, next to the 3rd Panzer Grenadier line
notes: Event date: CMH Lorraine Campaign ch. 2 p. 114: the new 3rd Panzer Grenadier line "extended from the left flank of the 17th SS Panzer Grenadier Division south of Sillegny". Event definition: the line of 17 September; the passage gives the division a flank at Sillegny, so the point is the flank and not the headquarters. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Sillegny with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: a line point. Location support: CMH names the village. Commander: unknown. Opponents: US 80th and 5th Infantry Divisions.
